decisions.reason: As a newly launched core drainage component with its own page and good fit to the firm's modular installation systems, it is worth keeping as a low-cost option while market acceptance becomes clearer.
Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's strategic direction, so despite limited website prominence the product should remain on the market until demand signals are better resolved.

This design-oriented shower drainage product matches the firm's value proposition for architects and design-conscious projects, and its dedicated presentation suggests enough commitment to continue learning before abandoning it.
A shower element with integrated slope strongly supports easier installation and renovation use cases, making it a strategically relevant option that should be kept open for now.

The backflow-protected basement drain addresses a clear technical problem with explicit launch positioning, so management would likely retain it while uncertainty is still early and the technology leverages existing drainage know-how.

The air-admittance valve appears more peripheral and was only lightly presented, but because it is still new and likely inexpensive to carry, the firm would probably keep it for another year rather than exit immediately.
